children: Three weeks after the $6.4 billion hack of global cryptocurrency exchange Binance, only $32 million has been recovered, equal to 0.5% of the total losses.

Blockchain investigator SomaXBT's analysis, cited by Wu Blockchain on Nov. 20, showed that about $2.82 billion of the stolen funds has been frozen, while $2.67 billion remains under the attacker's control. The amount actually recovered was just $32 million.
The attackers are still holding 18,270 Bitcoin stolen directly from Binance. Those holdings have not moved since the hack.

Some of the stolen funds, however, are being moved across multiple blockchains and trading services. According to SomaXBT, more than 5,100 Bitcoin was transferred through cross-chain liquidity protocol THORChain.
Another 1,482 Bitcoin was funneled into CoinJoin mixing transactions, which combine transaction records to make fund flows harder to trace. The kruw coordinator was used in most of that activity.

Transfers through THORChain and CoinJoin mixing are complicating efforts to trace and recover the stolen funds. The attacker's Bitcoin holdings are substantial, making any future movement a key focus.

A North Korea-linked hacking group has been identified as being behind the attack. The FBI previously determined that the Binance hack was carried out by TraderTraitor, a hacking group tied to North Korea.

Still, analyses released so far do not show when, or how much, of the frozen funds can actually be recovered. Frozen assets, funds still under the attacker's control and already recovered assets are separate categories, leaving the progress of the investigation and asset return process as the key issue.

title: Binance $6.4 Billion Hack Recovery Reaches Just $32 Million After Three Weeks
